summary.headline: Azad Engineering FY26 revenue rose about 30% to INR590 crores with 36.9% reported EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 25%+ growth on a ~INR6,500 crore order book.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR157 crores, up 26.4% YoY, with reported EBITDA margin of 36.7% and PAT margin of 22.3%. For FY26, standalone revenue was INR590 crores (consolidated INR603 crores) and PAT was INR132 crores standalone (INR134 crores consolidated), up about 54%. Management described FY26 as a year of consolidation and capacity build-out, with four dedicated lean facilities inaugurated since listing, and said inventory and working capital are elevated as plants ramp. Guidance for FY27 is 25%-plus top-line growth, with management saying this is conservative but would only be revised once the new plants stabilise.

segments.name: Energy and Oil & Gas (combined)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.5% of FY26 revenue, about INR481 crores, growing at least 34%; Q4 FY26 was INR128 crores (about 81% of quarterly revenue). Covers gas, steam and nuclear turbine components.

segments.name: Aerospace & Defence
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores for the first time; FY26 revenue about INR101 crores (transcript first said INR102 crores, corrected), about 17.2% of revenue, up roughly 25% YoY. Q4 FY26 contribution was INR28 crores.

segments.name: Oil & Gas
segments.commentary: Still largely in qualification; FY26 revenue under INR10 crores. Baker Hughes is the only customer named; management expects material revenue in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth of approximately 25%-plus for FY27, which management says applies to qualified products and is conservative; it may be revised upward after the new plants reach 100% stabilisation.

Order book of about INR6,500 crores (rolling, net of FY26 deliveries of about INR600 crores); management says it is 'INR6,500 crores plus' and expects roughly INR6,500 crores to be consumed over the next 5 years.
Inventory to fall to about 200 days in H1 FY27 and 160-170 days in H2 FY27.
About INR180-190 crores of the INR700 crore QIP proceeds remains to be deployed in FY27 capex.
Expected GST credit of about INR100 crores to be realised by H1 FY28.
EBITDA margin band remains 33%-35%-plus, per management.
capex_capacity: Four dedicated lean facilities inaugurated since listing: two in FY26, one in April 2026 (Baker Hughes), and one more earlier; ramp to committed throughput is the FY27 priority for GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi and Baker Hughes plants.
Of 8 planned dedicated facilities over 12-18 months, 4 are complete; management said it is on track for the remaining 4 by the end of FY27.
Saudi Arabia capacity with Baker Hughes is still planned but timelines have shifted; management is prioritising current plants.
Third plant (85,000 sq m) civil work has no start date; management says it follows ramp-up of current plants.
Heat treatment facility is NADCAP-approved; vacuum heat treatment is in-house, and more special processes are planned in-house.
demand_pricing: Order book split by segment: about $400 million Energy, about $200 million-plus Aerospace & Defence, about $100 million-plus Oil & Gas; individual customer values not disclosed.

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries awarded a single-source 8-year contract and purchase agreement for hot-section nozzle vane segments for gas turbine combustors; the part is new, previously made in-house by MHI, and value was not disclosed.
Aerospace airfoil qualification: Rolls-Royce first qualification batch expected in H2 FY26-27, with supply momentum from Q4 FY27 or early FY28; Pratt & Whitney and Safran to follow.
Management says growth comes from wallet-share gains on qualified parts, adjacent part numbers and horizontal deployment across customers.
Competitors named for hot-section work: Howmet Aerospace and PCC.
ATGG engine programme (national defence) is in delivery; management would not disclose order count or timelines, only that delivery is moving from years to weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM demand (GE, Mitsubishi, Siemens) make the 25% growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Chopdar said 25%-plus is a growth number that may be conservative, but a larger jump needs the new plants stabilised at 100%; he may revise it next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4 more dedicated facilities over 6 months on track?
Timeline to deliver the INR6,000 crore backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts run 5-6 years on average; management said about INR6,500 crores would be consumed over the next 5 years at 25%-plus growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is Oil & Gas material this year and what is the Energy vs A&D mix going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Oil & Gas revenue was under INR10 crores in FY26 and is expected to be material in FY27. Management expects Energy at 55-60% of revenue in five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Mitsubishi hot-section contract margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give contract economics or process details, and pointed to the top 2-3 global peers' profitability as a reference.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and cash flow being managed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory was built upfront for new plants and should convert to revenue from FY27, easing cash flow; about 96% of inventory is under one year old.

qa_highlights.question: Are capitalised product development costs in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said general development costs are expensed; only customer-specific tooling is capitalised.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory build and receivables of INR309 crores; inventory days target of 200 in H1 FY27 and 160-170 in H2 FY27 is key to watch.
Ramp-up risk on four new plants (GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi, Baker Hughes) and on the Rolls-Royce qualification batch in H2 FY27.
Execution risk on capacity, manpower and systems, which management identified as the main operating risks; a senior management restructuring is also under way.
Saudi Arabia Baker Hughes capacity timeline has slipped amid the Middle East conflict.
Oil & Gas ramp is from a very small base (under INR10 crores in FY26).
Other income of INR46 crores is expected to moderate as QIP funds go into capex; GST credit of about INR100 crores is pending realisation by H1 FY28.
Several investor questions were answered with 'we will talk offline' or 'visit the plant'; no contract economics for the MHI award were given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order visibility, but cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify the Mitsubishi contract, the ATGG programme and the Saudi project, and framed the FY27 growth figure as a floor that depends on plant stabilisation.
key_quotes: We are confident in sustaining strong business momentum and in delivering on our previously communicated top line growth of approximately 25% plus for the current year.

Capacity is largely in place. Qualifications are advancing across sectors and customers. Customer schedules are firm and are in place, and that's why we remain confident in delivering 25% plus top line trajectory, not just for FY '27, but on a multiyear basis.

It's important to note nearly 96% of our inventory is less than 1 year old, indicating that it is primarily linked to recent investment plant ramp-up, qualification requirements and customer-driven restocking needs rather than the legacy inventory.
So we are not dependent on any single customer or any geography or any single segment.

growth.why: Management reiterated approximately 25%-plus FY27 top-line growth, backed by a ~INR6,500 crore order book (about INR600 crore delivered in FY26) and 4 of 8 planned dedicated facilities complete with the rest targeted by end FY27; no utilisation figure given and the third plant has no start date.
